plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole avenues turn into drifts of lavender-violet as clouds of trumpet-shaped blooms cover the feathery-leaved branches. Petals fall to carpet streets and pavements in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late September through November (spring in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, and subtropical eastern Australia
plants.funFact: Native to South America, jacarandas were planted so widely in Pretoria that it is nicknamed the Jacaranda City. Tradition says a blossom landing on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub opens delicate, often fragrant flowers just as autumn gardens fade. Its blooms are single or semi-double, with golden stamens in the center, and they drop petals in soft drifts under the bush.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn into early winter, starting October–November and continuing through December or January
plants.location: Japan, where it is native, and in mild temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: It is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds are pressed for camellia oil, long used in Japan for hair and skin care.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: Dense, many-petaled flower heads in rich autumn shades light up gardens, temples and flower shows when most other blooms are over. Petals may be spiky, pom-pom round or spidery, depending on the cultivar.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, peaking in October and November
plants.location: Japan and East Asia, and gardens across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums bloom in response to shortening autumn days, a trait called short-day flowering. Growers exploit it by covering plants to trigger blooms at other times of year.
